reasons: Both addlist copies (boltons/dictutils.py and boltons/urlutils.py) now call `v = list(v)` before the emptiness check and before iteration. That materialises any iterable once, so generators, `iter(...)`, `map` and `filter` all work. Values stay in yield order, and an empty iterable returns early without creating the key. Lists, tuples and ranges behave as before. The only cost is a harmless extra copy for sequences. The only other changes are regression tests in tests/, which are small and within scope. I did not run the tests.
